title: What to Watch This Week: Akshay's Ghost, Suriya's God, and Imtiaz Ali's Broken Heart
excerpt: Seven picks across Netflix, Prime Video, JioHotstar, and theatres — plus exactly where the diaspora can watch each one. This week is absurdly stacked.
body:
Every now and then, the release calendar aligns in a way that makes your watchlist feel like a personal attack on your free time. This is one of those weeks. Between blockbusters hitting OTT, a Spielberg premiere, a partition love story with an AR Rahman score, and a 25-year-old cricket film returning to cinemas, there's genuinely too much to watch. Here are the seven titles worth your time — and where to find them if you're watching from outside India.

## 1. Bhooth Bangla — Netflix, June 12

**Akshay Kumar** and **Priyadarshan** reuniting for a horror comedy is the kind of nostalgia play that either works brilliantly or collapses under its own expectations. Bhooth Bangla — which grossed over ₹266 crore theatrically — falls closer to the former. Akshay plays a sceptic who inherits a cursed palace and decides to host his sister's wedding there, because apparently ₹266 crore worth of audiences enjoy watching a man argue with ghosts.

**Tabu** is the real draw here: effortlessly funny, perfectly timed, and doing the kind of work that reminds you why she's been irreplaceable for three decades. The palace setting is gorgeous, the scares are PG enough for family viewing, and Priyadarshan's comic timing hasn't rusted.

**Diaspora access:** Netflix worldwide. No geo-restrictions. This is your Thursday night sorted.

## 2. Karuppu — Prime Video, June 12

**Suriya** returned in god-mode and Tamil cinema collectively lost its mind. Karuppu, directed by RJ Balaji, earned ₹300 crore at the box office with a mass-action spectacle that's part mythology, part rage, part festival. The film positions Suriya in a rural avatar that's leaner and more ferocious than anything he's done in years. **Trisha Krishnan** co-stars, and the pair's chemistry crackles through every frame.

If you missed the theatrical run — or if you watched it in a packed Chennai hall and want to relive the whistles — Prime Video has you covered.

**Diaspora access:** Prime Video globally. Tamil with Hindi, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada dubs.

## 3. Main Vaapas Aaunga — Theatres, June 12

This is the one to watch for. **Imtiaz Ali** directing a partition love story with music by **AR Rahman** is already enough to buy a ticket, but the cast seals it: **Vedang Raina** and **Sharvari** as lovers separated across two timelines, with **Diljit Dosanjh** and **Naseeruddin Shah** bridging the gap. Early reviews are calling it Imtiaz's best work since Rockstar — which is either the highest praise possible or a very specific kind of heartbreak.

Rahman performed "Maa Tujhe Salaam" at the India-Pakistan border last week to promote the film, and honestly, if that doesn't make you emotional, I can't help you.

**Diaspora access:** Theatrical release in US, UK, Canada, and Gulf markets. Check your local listings — this one's getting a wide release.

## 4. Raakh — Prime Video, June 12

Set in Delhi in the late 1970s, **Raakh** follows the disappearance of two teenagers and the investigation that uncovers something far worse. **Ali Fazal** leads with a quiet intensity that's become his signature, and **Sonali Bendre** is back in a role that demands more than just star power. Director Prosit Roy (of Paatal Lok fame) builds atmosphere like few others in Indian cinema — slow, deliberate, and deeply unsettling.

This isn't a feel-good watch. It's a sit-in-the-dark-and-think watch. Perfect for anyone who's been craving an Indian crime drama with actual patience.

**Diaspora access:** Prime Video globally. Hindi with Malayalam and Tamil dubbed versions.

## 5. Disclosure Day — Theatres, June 12

**Steven Spielberg** making a film about alien contact is, in some ways, the most obvious sentence in cinema history. Yet Disclosure Day reportedly plays it straight — less spectacle, more paranoia, more of the quiet Spielberg who made Close Encounters. **Emily Blunt** leads, and the early buzz suggests this could be his most personal sci-fi since A.I.

For the diaspora: this is a global theatrical release, IMAX included, and India's getting it day-and-date with the US. No waiting.

**Diaspora access:** Wide theatrical release worldwide.

## 6. Dridam — JioHotstar, June 12

A Malayalam mystery thriller that flew under the radar deserves your attention. **Shane Nigam** plays a newly posted police officer who arrives in a sleepy Kerala village only to discover it's not sleepy at all. Murders, robberies, and local politics collide in what sounds like a South Indian True Detective riff. Director Martin Joseph Tharakunnel keeps the pacing tight and the atmosphere thick.

**Diaspora access:** JioHotstar. Malayalam with subtitles. You'll need the international plan.

## 7. Lagaan: 25th Anniversary Re-Release — Theatres, June 12

Twenty-five years ago, **Aamir Khan** convinced the world that a cricket match could be cinema. Lagaan remains the film that made international audiences take Indian cinema seriously — it was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, and if you've seen it, you know the nomination was the conservative call.

The re-release is digitally remastered, and if you've only ever watched it on a laptop, this is your chance to experience it the way it was meant to be seen: on the biggest screen you can find, with a crowd that knows every song.

**Diaspora access:** Limited theatrical re-release in select US, UK, and Australian cities. Worth hunting down.

---

**The verdict:** If you only have time for one, make it Main Vaapas Aaunga in theatres or Bhooth Bangla at home. If you have a full weekend, add Raakh and Lagaan and pretend the rest of your watchlist doesn't exist.
